topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the focus of the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Cellular Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and receptor systems through which the innate immune system detects microbial products and tissue injury to trigger an immune response.

topics.label: Inflammatory Signaling, Cellular Trafficking, and Systemic Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated sentinel cells direct the recruitment and migration of immune cells into tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the risks of runaway systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how unresolved responses lead to chronic inflammatory states.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic of the next lecture.
